definitions.explanation: The front part of the neck, including the internal passage for food and air.

examples.japanese: {喉|のど}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{渇|かわ}いた→渇く：10965_kawaku⟧。
{喉|のど}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}い→痛い：01108_itai⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
{喉|のど}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{赤|あか}く→赤い：00585_akai⟧⟦なっています→なる：01970_naru⟧。
⟦{風邪|かぜ}→風邪：02188_kaze⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引|ひ}いて→引く：01978_hiku⟧{喉|のど}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}い→痛い：01108_itai⟧。⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧⟦{食|た}べたくない→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I have a sore throat from a cold. I don't want to eat anything.

examples.japanese: {喉|のど}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{渇|かわ}いた→渇く：10965_kawaku⟧⟦ので→ので：09501_node⟧、⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}い→買う：00489_kau⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}きました→行く：00119_iku⟧。⟦{冷|つめ}たい→冷たい：00681_tsumetai⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦おいしかった→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: I was thirsty, so I went to buy water. The cold water was very refreshing.

notes:
{喉|のど} refers to the throat. The kanji {喉|のど} is complex, so it is frequently written in hiragana as のど.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {喉|のど}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{渇|かわ}く→渇く：10965_kawaku⟧: to be thirsty (literally 'throat dries')
- {喉|のど}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}い→痛い：01108_itai⟧: to have a sore throat
- {喉|のど}⟦{飴|あめ}→飴：00687_ame⟧: throat lozenge/drop
- {喉|のど}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{詰|つ}まる→詰まる：02079_tsumaru⟧: to choke, to get a lump in one's throat
- {喉|のど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{潤|うるお}す→潤す：08249_uruosu⟧: to wet one's throat, to have a drink

PROVERB:
⟦{喉|のど}もと→喉元：22093_nodomoto⟧⟦{過|す}ぎれば→過ぎる：01219_sugiru⟧⟦{熱|あつ}さ→熱さ：20971_atsusa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れる→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧ — 'Once past the throat, one forgets the heat.' Equivalent to 'Danger past, God forgotten.'

USAGE:
In Japanese, thirst is expressed as a throat sensation ({喉|のど}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{渇|かわ}いた→渇く：10965_kawaku⟧), not a stomach or body feeling as in some other languages.
